column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Article dates Nicocreon's suicide to 311 BC and the Ptolemaic governor; left out. Article says Arab destruction by Mu'awiya I (661-680); not printed. Article gives Evagoras 411-374 BC, consistent with desc (4th century).
Desc says secularisation 1802 and 1803; article says 1803 (mediatization). Written only as 1803 in the abbey's end... left as article. Desc 'Salem Castle' not in article.

Desc mentions the Salem Oak and treaty with the Lenape, not in article; not printed. Article says Fenwick 'laid out' 1675 consistent with desc 'founded 1675'. Article says Penn adjudicated; left. 'Fifth Tenth ~20%' omitted.
Desc mentions the Muntafiq confederation and the 1920 revolt; the article says neither, so not printed. Left out recent events (2016 bombing, 2006 clashes, cement/refinery figures 'as of 2007').
Article gives death 31 August 1158; summer 1158 used. Possible conflict: Sancho's reign described as one year, fine.

Desc says founded with American and Israeli help; article names French SDECE and CIA, no Israel: Israel not printed. Desc says dissolved after the revolution; article says closed shortly before the overthrow in February 1979: worded 'in 1979 as the monarchy fell'. Article also says CIA colonel 1953; the 1957 date for establishment given.
Desc says built mid-8th century; article construction 751-774, consistent. Article says 'said to have been built by Kim Daeseong' (desc states it plainly). World Heritage 1995 in desc, not repeated.

SKIPPED: a living political party: the article is almost all recent current affairs and assessments of present governments, with only a short settled history; desc and article also differ on recent events
SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance, and its reign dates (1273-1244 or 1265-1235 BC) are disputed

Desc says written in a modified Arabic-Urdu script since the 20th century; article says no single system, standardised late 2010s: the dates of first schemes (1960s) given only. Heading 'How it was used' used loosely for tone and vowels.
Article says Sacagawea guide; population figures varying not used. 2008 Bear River land purchase left out. Desc says Comanche split around 1700; article 'emerging as the Comanche by 1700'; fine.

Desc gives Foochow immigration from 1901 and the assassination of Governor Duncan Stewart in December 1949; the article gives neither, so not printed. Article mentions Wong Nai Siong without saying the settlement date.

Article gives two populations for 2013 (88,023 estimate; 77,926 survey): only the first printed. Desc says Zengids held it in the 12th and early 13th centuries: article Zengid branch 1171-1219, consistent. Left out 2017-2021 events and Ahmad Sanjar (list only).
Desc says Ahmad ibn Said was its governor before becoming imam in the 1740s: not in the article, not printed. Left out 2011 protests and investment figures.

Article gives two readings of slave proportion (a quarter to a half; at least half): neither fraction printed. Left out modern legacy items. Oyo mention in desc not in the article. Population 10-20 million (1837) omitted to keep length.

Desc says Mahmud sacked it in 1025; article says January 1026 and 1026, so no year printed. Desc says Ahilyabai 1783; article 'around 1783 (or 1785/1786)', so 'later 18th century' used. Desc says inaugurated 1951; article 'completed May 1951'. Article's 'Wikipedia text' about modern textbooks left out.

The article contradicts itself on the end of his presidency (lead: December 1975 to October 1986; body: until 1991, with Phoumi Vongvichit acting from 1986). Desc says 1991. No end date printed. Desc says he 'led' the Pathet Lao; article calls him a figurehead under Kaysone. Worded as the article has it.

Desc says the rising was led by the KPD; the article says some historians (Winkler, Haffner) hold the KPD neither wanted, planned nor led it. Not printed. Lead says death toll 150-200; body 156 (Prussian committee): only 156 printed.
Article does not say Gothic Revival 'largest such complex' except as piled warehouses; wording follows article. Left out 2005 goods figures and the Afghan Museum.
Desc says it granted charters to trading companies; article says only that it supervised them, so 'supervised'.
Article gives death 9 September 1727 after Ahmad Pasha's advance in autumn 1726; consistent. Omitted Russo-Persian War paragraph (thin) and the details of Mahmud's death.

Entry dates the reign c. 1344-1322 BCE, article c. 1350-1322 BC: reign start left out of the text. Article calls the heir Arnuwanda II in the family list but Arnuwanda I in the Zannanza section; text uses II. Article says first wife Henti may have been banished; omitted.

Article gives death 5 or 12 December 1112: day left out. Article says Tancred is usually misidentified as Italo-Norman (Hauteville only via mother; father possibly Aleramid); entry calls him Italo-Norman and says he 'styled himself prince' at Galilee, article says his coinage used servant of God / grand emir: text avoids both claims of ethnicity and the coin remark is stated as article has it (about regency of Antioch). Article has Tancred losing Galilee on becoming regent and recovering it 1109.

Article gives population as 33,000 in the lead and 28,000 in the knife-industry section: left out. Entry says Portuguese were shipwrecked and the local lord copied the guns; article says neither, so text does not say it.

Article says her sole reign 'could have lasted one to one and a half years ... now appears more likely about three': text gives about three, matching the entry. Article gives death 1188 BC; no death details. Article says Petrie dug the temple in 1896 and 1897: omitted. Manetho gives 7 years, consistent with entry.

Skipped rankings, student statistics, partnerships and recent prizes. Entry says it 'became a technical university in 1877'; article says Technische Hochschule 1877 and renamed Technische Universität in 1997: text says raised to Technische Hochschule in 1877.

Entry says Srivijaya dominated the straits seventh to thirteenth centuries and that thalassocracies needed less bureaucracy: article gives Srivijaya's emergence by the 7th century, subjugation c. 1275, and says nothing about bureaucracy; text follows article.
Hamilton's list gave him 63; Adair's attribution (1944) 51. Omitted No. 14, 39 and the Bill of Rights debate detail.
Article says first marriage 588; entry says 589: marriage year left out. Article lead says co-regent 616-626; body says Agilulf named her co-regent shortly before his death in 616.

Article's civil-war dates are December 1823 to February 1825; the entry says 1824-25: text gives only the March 1825 jailing. Article body says captured Tripolitsa in late 1821 (lead) but gives only 'Commander of the Greek forces during the Siege': text says led the forces in the siege.

Entry says 'a status no other country recognised'; article says South Africa recognised it, and later the other nominally independent homelands: text avoids it. Article gives the regional parliament as 45 elected of 109 and later 75 elected: only the first figure used.

Article says Alexander I ratified it 13 days before Napoleon's invasion, but also gives ratification 5 July 1812: the 13 days left out. Article says Selim III was deposed after early victories; omitted.

Article says the Dutch accepted the 1831 settlement in 1839 and 'regained the disputed territories' (consistent with entry). Neutral Moresnet paragraph is garbled and omitted. The Iron Rhine 2005 ruling omitted.
Article says Austria lost 400,000 subjects only in a quoted 1809 British comment; the entry's 'several million' is not in the article and is not repeated. Article also calls it the Treaty of Vienna.
Entry says Túpac Amaru 'broke off negotiations'; article says an Inca captain killed two Spanish ambassadors: text follows the article. Entry gives c. 1545 birth, article 14 April 1545.

Article gives death date as 26 August 1926 in the lead and 21 August 1926 in the Death section: day left out. 'The monarchy passed to his son' is inferred from 'in the lap of his eldest son' only: remove if flagged.
Entry says closed when the Soviet Army captured Königsberg in 1945; article says closed after the Potsdam Agreement transferred the city, campus 80% in ruins at the April 1945 capitulation.

Article's 'Ostrava' is only partly in Upper Silesia (eastern districts): text says larger cities; soften if flagged. Omitted post-1990 politics, statistics 'as of 2022', and the contested expulsion wording. Article gives pre-1138 Piast dates as 'By 990'.

Article says Urasoe was supplanted in the late 14th or early 15th century; entry says early 15th (Shō Hashi): text uses the article's range. Eiso and Satto and the Yōdore tomb link are in the entry, not named in the article text, so not repeated. Population as of 2024 left out.

Article gives the battle with Jahan Shah as Muş on 10 November 1467 (lead) and Chapakchur on 30 October or 11 November 1467 (Reign section): battle name and day left out. Article says Contarini was at his court 1473 to 1476. Ughurlu rebellion date not given.
Article gives death c. 600/609; entry c. 609; left vague. Article says born 530-540, entry c. 530.
Entry says Portuguese and French missionaries; article says Portuguese and Italian Jesuits (Pina, Rhodes of Avignon). Nationalities left out. Article gives 1620 for start; entry 17th century.
Entry says treatise title L'idea della architettura universale; article L'idea dell'architettura universale. Article's Teatro Olimpico dates 1584-85.
Entry says landing place of Kamehameha's fleet 1795; article only says capital 1795-96; omitted the landing. Present-day items (tourism revenue, 2017 erosion, homelessness) left out.
Entry says 'principal royal seat'; article says home to some of Maui's rulers. Mission station 'birthplace of sugar industry' phrase in article omitted.
SKIPPED: article has about 250 words of substance and mostly repeats the entry (Schönburg castle, pottery); too thin to add three sections

Article contradicts itself on founding (1849 by John Horse; 'city founded 1866' by Elijah Brown): city founding date left out, 1866 told as the return of refugees. Entry says Muscogee; article says Mvskoke (Seminole). Article's 2020 population given as 3,271 in lead and 3,133 in census section; used 3,133. Present-day crime/poverty/school scores omitted.

Entry says first Mercedes car of 1901; article: designed April-October 1900, prototype Dec 1900, racing 1901, released as Mercedes 35 hp in 1902. Dates left out. Entry 'from the 1880s' fits. Revival of the brand after 2002 omitted.
Entry mentions Monreale and Isaac Komnenos in Cyprus; not in the article, omitted. Entry says 'Cephalonia and Zakynthos'; article also Corfu, Ithaca.
Return year: article gives 125 BCE; entry 126 BCE. Death: article c. 114 BCE and 113 BCE; entry 113 BCE. Years omitted. The Wusun mission is dated 119-115 in article.
Article calls him proto-fascist in its own voice; attributed to Kieser instead. Entry says 'father of Turkish nationalism' (article too).
Article gives Mw 6.2 and 6.3 in different places; magnitude omitted. Rankings (fifth-deadliest, costliest) omitted. Spire not in the excerpt.
Entry's Pervane execution/Anatolia 1277 is not in the excerpt; omitted. Entry says 'Mamluk sultan Baybars invaded Anatolia 1277'; article says Baibars died 1277.

Entry says first since Egypt 1979 and Jordan 1994; article says the UAE and Bahrain were the first Arab League states to recognise Israel since Mauritania in 1995: that claim omitted. Developments after 2020 (Gaza war, new members) deliberately left out per the present-day rule.
Reign dates conflict between middle (1305-1274) and short chronology in the article; entry has the middle one, consistent; Qasr Shemamok inscription dated 1308-1275 in the article, left unstated.

Entry: Chalcis 'in about 50'; article: on the death of Herod of Chalcis in 48. Year left out. Death date disputed in article (c. 92 or 100); consensus before 93/94, entry c. 93: used the consensus wording only.
Entry: Shah-Armens ruled 1100-1207; article says their rule lasted until the 1230s (Jalal al-Din/Mongols): end date omitted. Entry says Armenian, Arab and Kurdish rulers before; fine.
Entry says studied law at Montpellier and Paris after which served at court; article: court post first, then studies in France. Told in article's order.
Entry says completed c. 1067; article says composed in 1068: date left out. Article is short (~500 words); text stays near the lower limit.
Article has no market price control details in the excerpt given beyond mention; kept to what is stated. Dates of Gujarat conquests (raid 1299, annexed 1304) used annex only.

Entry says Gisulf's duchy was the first Lombard duchy at Cividale; article agrees (Friuli). Entry dates: reign from about 560; article says 560-565 accession. Skull cup and Peredeo told as Paul's account.
Article uses BC/c. 76 BCE; entry d. 76 BCE, agrees. Article gives 27 years' reign and age 51 (not used). Josephus's two accounts of the death differ; left out.

Article gives no date for the Privilege of the Union (entry says 1287); left out. Article says he conquered the Kingdom of Majorca; I told Majorca, Ibiza, Menorca. Total length about 330 words (short article).

Article gives no year for Caonabo's capture (entry says 1495): left out. Return date of first voyage disputed in article: left out. Article says second voyage founded Santa Cruz 3 May 1502 (not used).
Article says An Lushan killed 29 January 757 after two years of rebellion; consistent. Article has no explicit Wikipedia-contradicting dates vs entry.
Article gives 1528 switch in June 1528, consistent with entry. Fieschi conspiracy 1547 agrees with entry.

Entry dates 1986-1989; article says operations officially 1988, February to August/September. I wrote 'began in February 1988' - this conflicts with entry's 1986-1989 range? Entry description says 'at its height in 1988'; kept to the article's phases. The Dutch court 2005 trial court said genocide, appeal 2007 said not: told only the 2007 appeal. Article names Dutch businessman only as Frans van Anraat; I did not name him.

Article: coup 1 April, entry says April; consistent. Entry says the Farhud followed; article doesn't use that word, I described the violence. Wavell's quote on Crete: told as hindering German reinforcements (Wavell's view); phrase 'prevented' attributed loosely, reconsider.
Article says nothing of the Tazeroualt or granaries (in the entry): not repeated. Article says 'average heights'. Article gives the range's length as approximately 500 km.
Article gives polio onset 1895 and paralysis January 1896; entry fine.
SKIPPED: article is about 310 words, mostly the lead and a name etymology; adds almost nothing to the entry's description
Article says Thessalus' story dated 493 BC about Kos; told as Thessalus's. Death legend told as legend.

Entry says Nasatyas invoked with Mitra, Varuna and Indra in the treaty: article does not say so, so I did not. Rigveda 'iron foot' = article says 'metal one'; I wrote 'iron foot' - fix to metal. Mare detail: Rigveda has Vivasvat and Saranyu, post-Vedic Sanjna.

Article makes strong claims (poet, 'true ruler', presided over council) from uncited accounts: left out. Article says 550-475 BC; entry c. 550-475 BCE agrees. Article says breast tumour was 'first recorded case of mastitis' - not repeated.
Article gives Ahmose's capture only as 16th century BC; entry says around 1550 BCE: left as 16th century. Entry says Fourteenth Dynasty seat: article does not mention.

Article dates birth c. 963; entry c. 960: birth year not printed. Article: Abkhazia accession 978 or 980; entry 978. Conquest of Kakheti: article says 'launched 1008, completed by 1010' vs entry 'in 1010 annexed' - consistent. Entry says David III 'kinsman': article father's cousin.
Entry says dynasty 'rising in Tao-Klarjeti in 9th century'; article gives 813 for Ashot I. Article's sentence 'Erekle II ... father Teimuraz' not used.

Entry says 'raiding as far as Delhi'; article: march to Delhi 1737 and Battle of Delhi 1737. Article's Deccan 1739-40 outcome is disputed between sources: left out. Mastani's marriage: article says relationship controversial, little known; I said 'gave him his daughter Mastani' as article does.

Headings for a work: used Origins / What it is / Discovery and study (guide list). Entry says 'designed to bypass Russia and Iran'; article says Russia declined; Iran not mentioned: not repeated. Present-day operator changes, ownership shares, contamination 2025 left out. Entry 'opened 2005' vs first oil at Ceyhan 2006: told both dates.
Article does not mention Vachagan III or the Albanian monarchy (in the entry): left out.
Article gives birth as c. 1910 and 29 March 1959; matches entry. Article says Boganda declared the republic on 1 December; entry says December 1958, consistent.
Article gives French force as 8,000 incl. 2,500 men-at-arms (lead) and elsewhere 3,000 knights and 4,000-5,000 infantry: totals left out. Flemish 9,400 (lead) vs 8,000-10,000: range used.

Article calls battle 'turning point' etc. Entry says Convention abolished monarchy 'the next day'; article says 'over the next two days' abolished monarchy and proclaimed republic: worded as article. Is Brunswick withdrawing 'soon' (entry) vs 30 September: kept date.

Article gives resignation 27 June 1827 in infobox/lead and 26 June 1827 in the text (Banda Oriental section); I used 27 June (lead, agrees with entry's 1827). Article also says he fled to exile 1829 / left for Spain after resigning.
Birth year given as 1389, 1395 or 1403 in the article (lead says 2 January 1403; entry 1403): birth year left out of text. Article's 'Council of Ferrara' heading vs Florence: used Ferrara-Florence.

Article length 279 km (3 Czech, 276 Polish) vs entry about 270 km: length left out. Article says river flows through Czech Republic and Poland; entry says Poland: mentioned source in Czech Republic only as location of source.
Article does not name Janamejaya, Kuru or Panchala; omitted. Brahmanas 'verse and prose' left out.
Omitted 2016 earthquake and economy claims (current-affairs / unsourced superlatives).
Article: Silla temple 'constructed in 751 begun by Kim Daeseong', completed 774; entry: begun mid-8th century. Consistent.

Article does not mention Wolio fortress, Makassar/Moluccas sea routes or the 16th-century adoption of Islam (entry claims); omitted. Article says sultanate ruled from 14th century; entry says Islam adopted 16th century: sultanate start date left out.

Article contradicts itself: plains annexed 14 Aug 1832, but Govinda Chandra's assassination dated 24 April 1840; entry says last king died 1830. All death dates left out. Etymology disputed in article (Gait vs Bhattacharjee); entry says name from Dimasa: etymology left out.
Entry says Mulberry mound site thought main centre of Cofitachequi: not in article, omitted. Article gives fourth oldest city / oldest inland city.

Entry says region became part of Hispania Tarraconensis; article says Hispania Citerior: province name omitted. Entry lists Cuenca among provinces; article lists Soria, Guadalajara, Zaragoza, Teruel only. Article's own date for Segeda revolt (155/154 BC) and Nobilior (153) not printed.

Article says Longcheng was capital 'through Later Yan and Northern Yan'; no date for Northern Wei conquest 436 or North Pagoda: omitted. 'Hongshan ruins' and 'Early Han period of 3rd century B.C.' - dated phrase omitted.

Article: 'Charles was released ... after Edward I's guarantees (Alfonso III released Charles)'. Entry says held until 1288: consistent with Canfranc Oct 1288. Article says Charles 'forced Jews to convert' - told plainly. Article says daughter Margaret married Charles of Valois, Blanche James II of Aragon, Maria Sancho I of Majorca: 'houses of Valois, Aragon and Majorca'.

Article says 'Count of Évreux beginning 1343'; entry just says count of Évreux. Article: Philip III father 'first cousin of Philip VI'. Death account from Blagdon 1803, a late retelling; Froissart cited in Cassell's version. Article says lead 'accidentally burned alive'.

Article gives return to Poland on '21 January' (no year) via Versailles; no year given for the Versailles transfer (the article says 21 January), so none printed. Article says Heidenreich 'resided and governed in Warmia 1245-1263'; entry says bishops resided at Löbau: residence left out. Gothic cathedral (entry) not described in article.
Article says first plenary 'elected the first government'; entry says elected Mao as chairman: left to 'first government'. Omitted present-day leader and CCP-supervision characterisations.

Article lists marriage to Theodora (Byzantine) before 1190, with bigamy rumours: not printed beyond the 1187 marriage. Article gives 28 April 1192 death; entry says 'days later' after April election: consistent.
Article calls treaty signed 'under threat of force'; 'ended seclusion' - entry same.
Article does not mention Ashanti; nothing said about it. Article's colony list table was not given.

SKIPPED: article is about daʿwah, Islamic proselytizing in general, mostly modern movements; the entry is the Ismaili/Fatimid da'wa institution, which the article covers in one sentence (organised in the 9th century by Isma'ilis)
Entry says born in Haarlem and working in Leuven from the 1440s; article says Leuven from 1457 (or possibly earlier) and gives no birthplace. Both points left out.

Entry says Ahmad Shah and his wife Turan Malik; article says it is often assumed they were married but there is no evidence of a marriage. Marriage left out. Recent restoration (2015-2024) left out as current affairs.
Birth date: article gives 17 October 1577 in the lead and 1 November 1578 in the body; entry says 1578. Birth date left out.

Founding date: article gives 37 BC (consistent with entry); other records cited in the article imply earlier dates; not printed. Entry says legend makes him son of Yuhwa and a heavenly father; article names Hae Mosu.
SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance (Roman capital of Novempopulania, cathedral of Saint Luperculus, Armagnac trade association, climate); adds little to the entry
Birth: article c. 1161, entry 1162; marriage: article 1170 (aged 9), entry 1177; neither year printed.

Entry says in Poland-Lithuania the whole nobility could take part; article says the election privilege was usually limited to magnates or officials in earlier periods; article does not describe the later electors, so the electors' extent is not stated. Entry's claim that the system 'weakened the state' not in article, not repeated.
Left out: GDP figures and the claim of largest growth of any president, foreign honours, the Nixon/Allende discussion.
Entry's 'reorganised finances and army' is not in the article; not repeated.
Birth: article gives 735 in the lead and 737 in the life events; entry says 737; birth year left out.

Birth: article c. 630 (entry c. 631); traditional sources 613 or 621; not printed. Jitō's accession given as 689 in the lead and 690 in the body: year left out. Entry mentions national histories; supplied excerpt only covers the law code.
Left out: rankings, economy share as of 2024, Woodward's report of payments.
Entry presents extraterritoriality as imposed on the Qing; article stresses that Qing negotiators readily granted it, in line with Qing practice. Both kept.
Thin article (about 300 words of substance); written short. Entry names Feurs as Loire town; article gives Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, not used.
Entry says Dahomey 'rose from early 17th century'; article says founded about 1620. Population percentages and notable living individuals left out.
Article contradicts itself on when the Classics entered the examinations (Han in the lead, Emperor Wu under Legacy, examinations begun in Sui); text avoids it.

Article gives area 302.4 km2 and 305.75 km2 (self-contradiction): left out. Left out tourism/festival detail and health claims about turnips. The Mongol refuge is only implied by the Goryeogung dates (article does not mention Mongols); not stated.

Desc says dam built 1907-1913; article gives only the closing of the gates on 27 June 1913, so I wrote that only. Droughts of 2023-2024 not in article; left out. 'Quarter as many ... as before' wording: article says 'only one quarter the number of native fish species were found'; kept close to it.

Desc says 'from 1468 until his death he fought Matthias Corvinus'; article puts Matthias joining the rebels after the excommunication of 23 Dec 1466 and his crowning on 3 May 1469: I gave no start year for the war. Article says 'Hungary, Poland, Bohemia, Bavaria, Brandenburg, Saxony, France, Burgundy and Italian states' as founding members; I named only a few. Article calls Ladislaus's guardian Frederick III 'as guardian of the young king'. Left out marriages and children.

Article says title 'lasted until the abdication of Wilhelm II was announced on 9 November 1918'; desc says abdication in November 1918: consistent. Article's text for the 1849 offer says the Frankfurt Parliament offered; the heading 'German Empire (1848-1849)' left out. Holy Roman Emperor sometimes also called 'German Emperor': left out.

Left out Vasari's claim that Ginevra appears in Ghirlandaio's fresco (article says Vasari was probably mistaken), the golden-ratio reconstruction of the hands and the 2017 anagram claim of Carla Glori. 'Wedding portraits were created in pairs' reasoning is the article's.

Article says the museum was 'originally built completely out of marble' while elsewhere implying brick: left out. Article's count of 18 sculptures in niches clashes with its list of figures: left out. Dates in BC/AD converted to BCE/CE.

Article's Strabo account (Cimmerians, Midas's suicide) left out to avoid the 800/700 BCE tension. Article gives both Yassıhüyük and Yassıhöyük spellings. Article says the Gordion Museum etc.; excavation 1950-1973 under Young, continued afterwards.

Desc gives about 2,500 km from Chittagong to Kabul; article gives about 3,655 km from Teknaf: length left out. Desc says Sher Shah rebuilt it 'in the 1540s'; article says only 16th century, so I wrote that. Article puts the Mauryan road in the 3rd century BCE alongside Chandragupta (conventionally earlier): I gave no century for Chandragupta. Kipling's passage paraphrased.

Article says clashes 'in 1896' and tensions receded; I kept brief. Article's armistice section: ceasefire 20 May; peace treaty 20 September. 'Wide autonomy' is the article's description. Left out Aromanian details.

Article gives conflicting dates for the 1925 rising (25 February; 21-27 February; conference 12 February) and conflicting terms on schools, and the name of the leader as Nele Kantule/Gantule: I gave only the month, the 4 March peace and 'Nele Kantule'. Desc says autonomy recognised in law 1938 and 1953: matches. Left out the 2020 governor item, 1983 plane crash, flag, Balboa and 1921 incident.

Desc says the Kumul Khanate lasted 'until 1930'; article gives no end date, so I gave none. Article says Hami 'repeatedly changed hands between the Chinese and Uyghurs' under the Later Han: doubtful, left out. Left out demographics, minerals, ICBM item.

Desc says 3rd and early 2nd millennium BCE; article says 2nd millennium BC: left out. Desc says no known relatives; article lists proposed links to Abkhazo-Adyghean, Kartvelian, Yeniseian, Burushaski and Kaskian: classification left out. Article says le- plural is disputed: left out.

Article gives two chronologies for his reign (c. 1275-1245 or 1267-1237 BCE); I gave neither, desc has the short one. Article's account of his governorship is muddled (Upper Land feud; 'King of the northern territories'): kept to 'governed the northern lands'. Left out the CTH list and the Year 34 marriage to Ramesses II's daughter.

Article's timeline says first documented mention 1225 'Castrum' while its text says 1214: I used 1214. Timeline gives French destruction 1688/1689; desc says 1689: I wrote 1689. The article text says upper castle destroyed 1537 (lightning, per timeline). Article is given only as lead and section openings; Nine Years' War section is empty, so the 1689/1693 wording follows the timeline and lead. Turner 'several times between 1817 and 1844'.

Desc says Trotha issued the extermination order on 2 October and Waterberg as a rout; article gives Waterberg 'in August' and no date for the first order (second order 22 April 1905): I gave no date for the first. Article says the Nama revolted in September 1904 (Witbooi). Left out 2021 settlement, reparations and historiography debate. Article's 'concentration camps' for all Herero after Wilhelm's order.

Article says Herod the Great executed his sons Alexander and Aristobulus IV in 7 BC; I wrote 'her father and his brother Alexander'. Desc calls Herod II 'Herod's son': the article calls him her half-uncle and Herod the Great's son by Mariamne: consistent. Article is inconsistent on whether Herod II was the first husband (possibly first wife of Archelaus): left out. Dates in BC/AD converted. 'Legacy' heading used as WRITER allows.

Article's dates 335-280 BC; desc c. 335 - c. 280 BCE: consistent. Article gives 'at least 600' vivisections claim from Celsus and Tertullian (disputed). Left out Skene's gland, ovum claims, calamus scriptorius, quote on health, later dissection history. Article says he credited with 'discovery of the ovum'; left out.

Article says Oviedo sacked in 794 (desc says 794 and 795): I wrote 794 only. Article calls Hisham both 'first son' and 'second son' of Abd al-Rahman, and gives age thirty at accession and forty at death (757-796 would be 31 and 39): ages left out. Horoscope tale attributed to 'one account' since the article states it without source.

Article says the League 'was dissolved after the Treaty of Karlowitz'; desc says 1684-1699: consistent. Article text calls Karlowitz peace made 'between the founding three members' and Russia not signing. Left out Hungarian secessionist conspiracy, Persia details, Sobieski's death. 'Refusal to surrender' paraphrases 'prolong the Ottoman surrender'.

Desc says 'created in 1815', 'directly elected since 1848' and 'PR since 1956'; article gives only the seating 1815-1992, the 100 to 150 seats change in 1956 and PR from 1917: I stated no creation date, no 1848, and PR only 'in its present form in 1917'. Article says 'Between 1815 and 1992' seated in the ballroom. Left out voter eligibility, EU role, renovation.
Article names the Polish kings only as 'two Wettins were Kings of Poland (1697-1763)'; I did not name them. Present-day headship disputes and living agnates left out.
Article says rediscovered 1501 and also discovered 1493/94 by Celtis: I gave 1493 or 1494 only. Death date left out (article 973, entry c. 973).
Article has birth 'before 1527'; entry c. 1503. Left out.

Article gives East Gate reconstruction as 1975 and 1978, and the main reconstruction as 1970 and 1970s: I wrote 1970s only. Section heading 'Discovery and study' is the nearest allowed heading for construction records and restoration. Fires and festivals of recent years left out. Article says wall designs 'attributed' - it says 'according to the designs of the architect'; entry says Jeong Yak-yong helped design cranes; consistent.
SKIPPED: article about 200 words of substance; mostly repeats the entry (Parthenon, Bassae, Eleusis)

Article calls fables 'for villagers' - 'To the Children' preface; kept. Dating of fable audience '1735-1801' in article is garbled; not used. Epic 'Wojna chocimska' about Khotyn War - not named to avoid new link issues.
